title: Democratic Preference Alignment via Sortition-Weighted RLHF

bias_targets.methodology: Evaluating downstream model alignment against constitutional principles elicited from a representative public. The study compares models trained on preference data from a biased, self-selected convenience sample of human raters against models trained using sortition-weighted RLHF that enforces demographic quotas across ethnicity, religion, marital status, education, employment status, gender, and age.

Measuring the Pearson correlation between the presentation order of candidate responses and their final rank assigned by the LLM-as-a-judge, as well as calculating the probability that a response at a specific position is ranked first.

Correlating model response length (measured in both characters and words) with the ranking assigned by the LLM-as-a-judge, and computing the win rate of longer responses in implied pairwise comparisons to verify that evaluation preferences are not strictly driven by length.
